descStruct.summary: THE INERTIAL-DETERMINACY VERSION OF MERCURY AND THE SUN (wave 295c; the originator's ruling in report 85; the coordinator's check item R155). ☄️ mercuryReal's real-unit Sun (pinned) and Mercury (masses, radii, positions, speeds and spins copied without a single change) run under gravity (E4) and the INERTIAL DRAG (the default composition rule solve(velocity)). geoPN=3 (the mark for enabling the inertial-determinacy drag - geodesic off, no 1PN), kFrame=0. THE GAIN IS 🌛 earthMoonInertial's 514182 CONVERTED AS THE SAME SI COEFFICIENT 0.0514182 m^3/kg INTO 51.4182 [L^3/M] (1 unit = 10^8 m / 10^4 s / 10^27 kg): a transfer, fitted neither to the perihelion advance nor to the period. The kernel softening eps equals ☄️'s gravitational softening 0.05 (= 5e6 m). The Sun and Mercury are points (no internal core is declared). THE 43 ARCSEC/CENTURY IS A 1PN QUANTITY AND NOT THE AIM OF THIS SAMPLE (it has no 1PN). Measured (harness tests/exp-w295c-inertial3.mjs, 8 orbits, h=0.016 and h/2): the perihelion turns prograde by 0.3279 deg per orbit (~4.90e5 arcsec/century), against -9 arcsec/century for the gain-0 control (the softening's retrograde term). The period is 87.892 d (gain-0 control 87.969 d; -0.088%). The mean |u|/|v| is 5.62e-4. THE LIMIT OF THE INPUT-VELOCITY MAPPING: ☄️'s vx/vy are given to the dynamical velocity v as they are (x-dot = v + u), so the perihelion coordinate speed is not the observed 58.98 km/s (this is not a comparison with the observed coordinate speed). The numbers are a record, not a pass/fail verdict.
descStruct.observe: Use the trail and the ghost ellipses (dotted = initial, amber = precession x20) to watch the perihelion turn prograde by about 0.33 deg per orbit (with gain 0 it stays still). The eccentricity proxy is 0.20488 (gain-0 control 0.20563). The HUD time is shown in days.
descStruct.control: The one-tap control is gain 0 (the inertial drag off - ☄️'s gravity-only two-body system; with geoPN 3 there is no 1PN either). The 1PN perihelion advance is seen in ☄️. The gain is not lowered towards 43 arcsec/century (it is the declaration transferred from 🌛). Halving dt moves the apsidal rate by 1.4e-6 deg/orbit.

descStruct.summary: THE INERTIAL-DETERMINACY VERSION OF THE SUN, EARTH AND MOON (wave 295c; the originator's ruling in report 85; the coordinator's check item R155). 🔆 emAuditSolar's real-unit Sun (pinned), Earth and Moon (masses, radii, positions, speeds and spins copied without a single change) run under gravity (E4) and the INERTIAL DRAG (physics.relativeDrag.law:"inertial"; the default composition rule solve(velocity) solves (I+L)u = s from the dynamical-velocity differences and moves positions only, x += u dt). geoPN=3 (the mark for enabling the inertial-determinacy drag - geodesic off, no 1PN), kFrame=0. THE GAIN IS 🌛 earthMoonInertial's 514182 (1 unit = 10^6 m / 10^2 s / 10^25 kg) CONVERTED AS THE SAME SI COEFFICIENT C_d,SI = 0.0514182 m^3/kg INTO 51.4182 [L^3/M] (1 unit = 10^8 m / 10^4 s / 10^27 kg): a transfer, not a fit - nothing is refitted here to the apsidal period or the sidereal month (🌛's gain is itself an estimate from a one-dimensional fit of the apsidal period). THE DRAG PAIR IS THE EARTH-MOON PAIR ONLY (pairs:[[1,2]] - the Sun is a gravitational third body only and is kept out of the drag sum). The Earth declares 🌛's starting structure core dragCore:{massFrac:0.325, radius:0.0348} (= 3.48e6 m); the Sun and the Moon are points. The kernel softening eps equals this sample's gravitational softening 0.01 (= 10^6 m - ten times 🌛's kernel eps of 10^5 m). Measured (harness tests/exp-w295c-inertial3.mjs, output tests/out/inertial3-w295c.json; the 118-orbit window was declared before measuring): the apsidal period is 4.727 yr over 27 orbits and 4.262 yr over 118 orbits, shorter than the drag-off control (gain 0 = 🔆's gravity-only three-body system) at 8.778 yr - the drag's advance adds to the solar perturbation's. The period per 27 orbits moves with the window, 4.727/4.618/4.549/4.305 yr (not called steady). The numbers are a record, not a pass/fail verdict.
descStruct.observe: Use the trail and the ghost ellipses (dotted = initial, amber = precession x20) to watch the Moon's apse line turn prograde. The camera follows the Earth with a +/-10-unit field (as in 🔆). Over 118 orbits the sidereal month is 27.139 d and the eccentricity proxy 0.0322 (the gain-0 control: 27.319 d, 0.0374). The RMS residual of the straight-line fit of the apse direction is 25.5 deg (the solar wobble of the apse - short-window rates wobble and are not read). The HUD time is shown in days and years.
descStruct.control: The one-tap control is gain 0 (the inertial drag off - 🔆's gravity-only three-body system with geoPN 3). The other control, A2 (pairs:"all" - the Sun is a drag source too; the pinned Sun keeps u = 0 yet acts as a source, and sum m u does not close), runs only inside the harness: 4.261 yr over 118 orbits (-2.6e-4 from the declared A1). The declaration stays A1 (A2 is not made the default). Halving dt moves the 118-orbit apsidal period by 5.7e-4. The two-body version without the Sun is 🌛; the three-body system without the drag is 🔆.

en.name: Earth & Moon

descStruct.summary: A two-body demo with the Moon orbiting Earth (cores calibrated to observed values). The mass ratio is the real one: mMoon/mEarth=0.0123. The Moon rotates synchronously — its spin equals the measured orbital angular velocity ω=0.013908, so the same face of its spoke wheel always points at Earth (tidal locking).
descStruct.observe: Cores use observed values: Earth Mc/m=0.325 (PREM whole-core mass fraction) and Moon Mc/m=0.0168 (lunar-laser-ranging median of 1.59–1.77%). Core v2's mode="rigid" (the core co-rotates with the shell, Ω_c≡s) is the neutral default — Earth's inner-core differential rotation relative to the mantle varies with the period and method of estimation and is not established as a fixed ratio, so this sample adopts rigid rotation as its neutral default (no differential = exactly equivalent to a single layer). The circular-orbit speed is calibrated with E6′ included: v=1.063× Keplerian (Plummer-softened) — radius drift 0.09% over 4 orbits with sync maintained. Earth's spin (0.05) is calibrated into the E6′-stable regime — at the real ratio (27.4× the Moon's) the drag wind exceeds gravity (E4) and the orbit collapses (measured). Earth is pinned (exhibit system). κ=1×10⁻⁴ (legacy notation Kt=10000) satisfies the GR-calibration lock κ=G/c².

For the real spin ratio, see 🌕 (free two-body, kFrame=0). For the real-scale calibration (real G and real c, real distances and masses, reproducing the 27.32-day sidereal month) see 🌙 (real units, kFrame=0) and 🌘 (real units, kFrame=1 — the template calibrated all the way to the 8.85-year apsidal precession); this sample is not a calibration but a storytelling toy whose only observed-value fit is the core mass fraction.

descStruct.summary: A two-body problem where neither Earth nor the Moon is pinned — everything is measured from their shared center of mass.
descStruct.observe: With kFrame=0 (pure Newtonian control) spin does not affect orbits, so the REAL spin ratio can be used directly: Earth spin=0.3609 (27.4× the Moon's orbital rate — the actual ratio) and the Moon rotates synchronously at spin=ω=0.013174. descStruct.summary: 氷の粒でできた土星の環を再現するサンプル。240個の氷粒(3つの環帯・60/120/60個、軽くて衝突でもエネルギーをあまり失わない muF=0.2/γN=0.15)を配置し、中心星のスピンが空間を引きずる(kFrame=1・A8空間の引きずり)条件のもとで、長時間安定な環になるかを見る。初期配置は t=300〜600 で落ち着いた分布に合わせてある。
descStruct.observe: 実測(環240粒の新構成): t≈360 で帯内(90≤r≤290)97.1%・落下(r<85)1粒/240・散逸(r>320)0、t≈1200 でも帯内98.8%・落下1粒・散逸0(QA behavior.saturnExp)。※安定の理由づけは実測に合わせて弱めてある: 同一初期配置で kFrame だけを 0 にした対照(3000步)でも環は100%保たれ、離心率RMSはむしろ小さい(0.063 対 kFrame=1 の 0.142)。引きずりは環を内側へ寄せ(帯中央値 159 対 171)離心率を上げる向きに効いており、「引きずりが環を円くして保つ」とは言えない(QA behavior.saturn-kframe-control)。摩擦 muF も、氷粒の半径 R=rMul·√m≈0.18〜0.31 が環の半径域 104〜212 に対して極小で接触がまれなため、この時間窓ではほとんど効かない — 3000步では muF=0.2/0/1.0 の3本が倍精度で完全一致し、6000步でも muF=0 との差は平均|spin| 1.7%・離心率RMS 0.02% にとどまる(QA behavior.saturn-muf-control)。κ=1/3600(旧表記 Kt=3600)は物理対応ロック κ=G/c² の成立値。中心天体の表示半径は個体半径倍率 rMul=1.8 で環との見かけの比率が近くなるよう調整している。
descStruct.control: おすすめA/Bは kFrame=1⇄0(環の内向き移動と離心率の差)。実在天体との照合の近点移動は 📡 を参照。

en.name: Saturn's Rings (Experimental)

descStruct.summary: A sample reproducing Saturn's icy rings. 240 icy grains (three bands of 60/120/60; low mass, low energy loss on collision: muF=0.2/γN=0.15) are set up under a condition where the central star's spin drags nearby space (kFrame=1, A8 frame dragging), to see whether the ring stays stable over time. The initial layout matches the settled distribution measured at t=300–600.
descStruct.observe: Measured (the new 240-grain build): at t≈360, 97.1% stay in the band (90≤r≤290), 1 grain of 240 falls (r<85) and none escape (r>320); even at t≈1200 it is 98.8% in band, 1 fallen, 0 escaped (QA behavior.saturnExp). Note that the account of WHY it is stable has been weakened to match the measurements: with the same initial layout and only kFrame switched to 0, the ring is still 100% retained after 3000 steps and its RMS eccentricity is in fact LOWER (0.063 vs 0.142 at kFrame=1). Dragging pulls the ring inward (band median 159 vs 171) and raises eccentricity, so it cannot be said that dragging keeps the ring round (QA behavior.saturn-kframe-control). Friction muF barely acts either: the grain radii R=rMul·√m≈0.18–0.31 are tiny against the 104–212 ring span, so contacts are rare — at 3000 steps muF=0.2, 0 and 1.0 agree to full double precision, and even at 6000 steps switching muF off changes mean |spin| by only 1.7% and RMS eccentricity by 0.02% (QA behavior.saturn-muf-control). κ=1/3600 (legacy notation Kt=3600) satisfies the GR-calibration lock κ=G/c²; the central body's displayed radius is tuned with the per-body radius multiplier rMul=1.8 so its apparent proportion to the ring stays close.
descStruct.control: Suggested A/B: kFrame 1 vs 0 (inward migration and the eccentricity difference). See 🛰️ for the observed-body comparison of the apsidal precession.
descStruct.brief: Measure whether a ring of ice grains survives a long run. Met: 97.1% stay in the band and 0.4% fall in, within the gate. Out of calibration scope.

descStruct.summary: 🪐 土星の環の姉妹版 — 中心星に**コア(核)**を入れ(コアv2・質量比 Mc/m=0.18・全体の質量 1500 は不変)、**コアと殻の差動 Ω_c−s だけが追加の空間引きずり(A8)として環に効く**ことを見る。**効き目は「あるが微弱」が正直な結論**: 剛体回転(mode="rigid"・差動ゼロ)との帯中央値差は t≈150 で 0.036(QA behavior.saturnLayered)。環は 🪐 と同一(氷粒 240・3帯 60/120/60)で、衝突円形化(T3)も同じ。
descStruct.observe: コア質量比 18% は Cassini 後の重元素集中の推定(≈17地球質量/95地球質量)を参考にした値。コア半径比 Rc/R=42% は旧既定写像 Rc/R=√|Mc/m| により質量比から算出したモデル内値で、観測されたコア境界半径ではない(環震学では重元素勾配領域が半径約60%まで広がるモデルが示されている)。コアv2 は独立した角運動量 J_core を持ち、コア角速度 Ω_c と殻スピン s の差動分だけが ω += (Mc/m)·(Ω_c−s)·f(Rc,d) としてコア核 Rc から追加の空間引きずり(A8)に効く(既定 Ω_c=0.0525=1.05×0.05 は差を見やすくする教材用の仮定値。土星深部の回転は観測・モデル依存で、コア対表層のスピン比としては確定していない。mode="rigid" が剛体回転=差動ゼロの中立対照)。コアスピンは熱・散逸(T3/E10′)と切り離された固定内部回転源(反作用で変化しない外部拘束)であり、閉じた2層天体ではなく統制実験である点に注意。氷粒の衝突円形化(T3)は 🪐 と同一。

en.name: Saturn's Rings (Two-Layer Primary)

descStruct.summary: A sister sample to 🪐 Saturn's Rings, giving the central star an inner 'core' (Core v2 — mass fraction Mc/m=0.18; the total mass m stays 1500) to see that ONLY THE CORE–SHELL DIFFERENTIAL Ω_c−s adds frame dragging (A8) on the ring. THE HONEST CONCLUSION IS 'PRESENT BUT FAINT': the band-median difference against rigid rotation (mode="rigid", zero differential) is 0.036 at t≈150 (QA behavior.saturnLayered). The ring is identical to 🪐's (240 icy grains in three bands of 60/120/60) and so is the collisional circularization (T3).
descStruct.observe: Measured: at t≈360, 96.7% in band, 1 grain of 240 fallen, none escaped, band medians 114/144/198; the band-median difference against rigid rotation (mode="rigid") is 0.036 at t≈150 (QA behavior.saturnLayered). The core mass ratio Mc/m=0.18 is chosen to reference post-Cassini estimates of heavy-element concentration (≈17 of 95 Earth masses). Rc/R=42% is a model-internal value derived from that mass ratio by the legacy default mapping Rc/R=√|Mc/m| — not an observed core-boundary radius (ring seismology instead points to a heavy-element gradient region extending to roughly 60% of the radius). Core v2 gives the core its own angular momentum J_core, and only the differential between the core's angular velocity Ω_c and the shell spin s adds frame dragging (A8) through the smaller core kernel: ω += (Mc/m)·(Ω_c−s)·f(Rc,d). The default Ω_c=0.0525 (=1.05×0.05) is a teaching assumption chosen to make the contrast visible; Saturn's deep-interior rotation is observation- and model-dependent, and a core-vs-envelope spin ratio is not established (mode="rigid" is the rigid-rotation neutral control). The core spin is a fixed internal rotation source decoupled from heat and dissipation (T3/E10′) — a controlled experiment, not a closed two-layer body. en.description: A sister sample to 🪐 Saturn's Rings, giving the central star an inner 'core' (Core v2 — mass fraction Mc/m=0.18; the total mass m stays 1500) to see that ONLY THE CORE–SHELL DIFFERENTIAL Ω_c−s adds frame dragging (A8) on the ring. Measured: at t≈360, 96.7% in band, 1 grain of 240 fallen, none escaped, band medians 114/144/198; the band-median difference against rigid rotation (mode="rigid") is 0.036 at t≈150 (QA behavior.saturnLayered). The core mass ratio Mc/m=0.18 is chosen to reference post-Cassini estimates of heavy-element concentration (≈17 of 95 Earth masses).
